back: 50% of purchase or short sale value for equities.
spoken: Reg T initial margin for stocks is fifty percent.

back: Settlement cycle + 2 business days: T+3 (S+2) under T+1 settlement.
spoken: Reg T payment is due two business days after settlement. Under T plus one, that's T plus three.

back: $2,000. Long purchase: deposit the lesser of cost or $2,000. Short sale: always at least $2,000.
spoken: The FINRA margin minimum is two thousand dollars. For a long buy, deposit the lesser of the cost or two thousand. For a short sale, always at least two thousand.

back: Long: 25% of LMV. Short (stock $5 or more): 30% of SMV.
spoken: Minimum maintenance is twenty-five percent long and thirty percent short.

back: Debit / 0.75 (per share: divide by shares).
spoken: Long account maintenance call: divide the debit by point seven five.

back: Credit / 1.30.
spoken: Short account maintenance call: divide the credit balance by one point three.

back: Equity - (50% x LMV). Credited to SMA.
spoken: Excess equity is equity minus fifty percent of market value. It goes to SMA.

back: SMA x 2 (at 50% Reg T).
spoken: Buying power is SMA times two.

back: A decline in market value. SMA falls only when used.
spoken: A falling market doesn't reduce SMA. Only using it does.

back: Equity below 50% Reg T: 50% of sale proceeds released to SMA.
spoken: In a restricted account, half of any sale proceeds goes to SMA.

back: FINRA replaced the pattern day trader rules and $25,000 minimum with risk-based intraday margin standards, effective June 4, 2026 (phase-in through Oct 20, 2027). Exam material may lag; verify.
spoken: In June twenty twenty-six, FINRA replaced the pattern day trader rule and its twenty-five thousand dollar minimum with intraday margin standards, phased in through October twenty twenty-seven. Prep materials may still test the old rule.

back: T+1 for stocks, corporate and municipal bonds (since May 28, 2024); Treasuries T+1.
spoken: Regular way settlement is T plus one for stocks, corporates and munis since May twenty twenty-four.

back: Same business day as the record date.
spoken: Under T plus one, the ex-date is the same day as the record date.

back: Buy stop: above market, protects shorts. Sell stop: below market, protects longs.
spoken: Buy stops sit above the market and protect short sellers. Sell stops sit below and protect long positions.

back: An order to buy or sell immediately at the best available price, which guarantees execution but not price.
spoken: Market order. An order to buy or sell immediately at the best available price, which guarantees execution but not price.

back: An order to buy at or below, or sell at or above, a set price, which guarantees price but not execution.
spoken: Limit order. An order to buy at or below, or sell at or above, a set price, which guarantees price but not execution.

back: An order that becomes a market order once the stock trades at or through the stop price.
spoken: Stop order. An order that becomes a market order once the stock trades at or through the stop price.

back: An order that becomes a limit order once the stop price is reached.
spoken: Stop-limit order. An order that becomes a limit order once the stop price is reached.

back: An order that must be filled completely or not at all, though not necessarily immediately.
spoken: All-or-none order. An order that must be filled completely or not at all, though not necessarily immediately.

back: An order that must be executed immediately and in full, or it is canceled.
spoken: Fill-or-kill order. An order that must be executed immediately and in full, or it is canceled.

back: An order that must be executed immediately, with any unfilled part canceled.
spoken: Immediate-or-cancel order. An order that must be executed immediately, with any unfilled part canceled.

back: An order giving the representative discretion over the time and price of execution.
spoken: Not-held order. An order giving the representative discretion over the time and price of execution.

back: An order to be executed at or as near as possible to the closing price.
spoken: Market-on-close order. An order to be executed at or as near as possible to the closing price.

back: An order that stays open until it is executed or canceled.
spoken: Good-till-canceled order. An order that stays open until it is executed or canceled.

back: A quote at which the dealer is obligated to trade at least the stated size.
spoken: Firm quote. A quote at which the dealer is obligated to trade at least the stated size.

back: A quote that needs reconfirmation before the dealer will trade on it.
spoken: Subject quote. A quote that needs reconfirmation before the dealer will trade on it.

back: An approximate price range for a trade that needs special handling, such as a large block.
spoken: Workout quote. An approximate price range for a trade that needs special handling, such as a large block.

back: The Reg SHO rule that a firm must borrow or have reasonable grounds to believe it can borrow a security before accepting a short sale.
spoken: Locate requirement. The Reg SHO rule that a firm must borrow or have reasonable grounds to believe it can borrow a security before accepting a short sale.

back: A firm's duty to use reasonable diligence to get the most favorable terms reasonably available for customer orders.
spoken: Best execution. A firm's duty to use reasonable diligence to get the most favorable terms reasonably available for customer orders.

back: Standard settlement one business day after trade date for stocks, corporate and municipal bonds, and Treasuries.
spoken: Regular-way settlement. Standard settlement one business day after trade date for stocks, corporate and municipal bonds, and Treasuries.

back: Same-day settlement, with delivery due by 2:30 PM Eastern time if the trade is executed before then.
spoken: Cash settlement. Same-day settlement, with delivery due by two:thirty PM Eastern time if the trade is executed before then.

back: A trade in a security that has been approved for issue but not yet issued, settling on a date set after issuance.
spoken: When-issued trade. A trade in a security that has been approved for issue but not yet issued, settling on a date set after issuance.

back: A document a seller gives to a buyer to show the buyer is owed a dividend or distribution received by the seller.
spoken: Due bill. A document a seller gives to a buyer to show the buyer is owed a dividend or distribution received by the seller.

back: A separate assignment form that transfers ownership of a stock certificate without signing the certificate itself.
spoken: Stock power. A separate assignment form that transfers ownership of a stock certificate without signing the certificate itself.

back: Delivery of securities in proper form, with correct denominations, signatures and endorsements, so the buyer must accept it.
spoken: Good delivery. Delivery of securities in proper form, with correct denominations, signatures and endorsements, so the buyer must accept it.

back: A book-entry system that lets investors hold shares in their own names on the issuer's records without a physical certificate.
spoken: Direct Registration System. A book-entry system that lets investors hold shares in their own names on the issuer's records without a physical certificate.

back: A DK, sent when a firm does not recognize a trade a contra-party has reported.
spoken: Don't know notice. A DK, sent when a firm does not recognize a trade a contra-party has reported.

back: The right to return securities previously accepted when a delivery problem is later discovered.
spoken: Reclamation. The right to return securities previously accepted when a delivery problem is later discovered.

back: The first day a stock trades without the right to the upcoming dividend, which is the record date under T+1 settlement.
spoken: Ex-dividend date. The first day a stock trades without the right to the upcoming dividend, which is the record date under T plus one settlement.

back: FINRA's system for reporting over-the-counter trades in corporate and agency bonds and certain other debt.
spoken: TRACE. FINRA's system for reporting over-the-counter trades in corporate and agency bonds and certain other debt.

back: The MSRB's real-time transaction reporting system for municipal securities trades.
spoken: RTRS. The MSRB's real-time transaction reporting system for municipal securities trades.

back: The MSRB website that publishes municipal trade prices and disclosure documents for free.
spoken: EMMA. The MSRB website that publishes municipal trade prices and disclosure documents for free.

back: A FINRA facility for reporting off-exchange trades in exchange-listed stocks.
spoken: Trade reporting facility. A FINRA facility for reporting off-exchange trades in exchange-listed stocks.

back: The NYSE member responsible for maintaining a fair and orderly market in assigned stocks.
spoken: Designated market maker. The NYSE member responsible for maintaining a fair and orderly market in assigned stocks.

back: A trading halt across all markets triggered by large declines in the S and P 500, at levels of 7, 13 and 20 percent.
spoken: Market-wide circuit breaker. A trading halt across all markets triggered by large declines in the S and P five hundred, at levels of seven, thirteen and twenty percent.

back: A trade in which the firm buys from or sells to the customer from its own inventory, charging a markup or markdown.
spoken: Principal transaction. A trade in which the firm buys from or sells to the customer from its own inventory, charging a markup or markdown.

back: A trade in which the firm acts as broker between buyer and seller, charging a commission.
spoken: Agency transaction. A trade in which the firm acts as broker between buyer and seller, charging a commission.

back: A written grievance by a customer about a representative or firm, which must be kept on record and reported to a principal.
spoken: Written complaint. A written grievance by a customer about a representative or firm, which must be kept on record and reported to a principal.

back: A binding dispute resolution process before a FINRA panel, with very limited grounds for appeal.
spoken: Arbitration. A binding dispute resolution process before a FINRA panel, with very limited grounds for appeal.

back: A voluntary, non-binding process in which a neutral mediator helps the parties settle.
spoken: Mediation. A voluntary, non-binding process in which a neutral mediator helps the parties settle.

back: The uniform registration form for representatives, which must be updated for events such as certain customer complaints, liens and criminal charges.
spoken: Form U4. The uniform registration form for representatives, which must be updated for events such as certain customer complaints, liens and criminal charges.

back: The termination notice a firm files when a representative leaves, due within 30 days.
spoken: Form U5. The termination notice a firm files when a representative leaves, due within thirty days.

back: Correcting an error by canceling a trade and rebooking it in the right account, which requires principal approval.
spoken: Cancel and rebill. Correcting an error by canceling a trade and rebooking it in the right account, which requires principal approval.

back: An incorrect trade report sent to a customer, which does not bind the firm to the wrong price.
spoken: Erroneous report. An incorrect trade report sent to a customer, which does not bind the firm to the wrong price.
